submission.natural_language_explanation: L15/N1229- is a register detector for text written in an institution's own voice: it rises over a whole passage of corporate, administrative or technical self-description - mission and values statements, product and press-release claims, business reporting, official notices, reference entries, and code or markup - and peaks on whichever token in that passage carries most of the register (an abstract evaluative word such as 'excellence' 1.54, 'innovation' 1.40, 'seamless' 0.85 or 'integrity' 0.77; a formally specified value such as the year in 'The bridge was built in 1893' 0.30 or the times in 'from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.' 0.23; or the closing bracket or tag of a code entry, ')' 0.31 and '></' 0.24). The same content in plain speech or personal narration falls to the floor - 'We deliver excellence across every engagement' 1.54 vs 'We do good work for our clients' 0.08, 'Our team values integrity above all' 0.77 vs 'He questioned her integrity' 0.01, 'The committee reviewed the documents' 0.29 vs 'The children found the documents' 0.16, and a three-sentence personal passage peaks at 0.19-0.25 against 1.46-1.66 for a corporate one - and the mechanism is retrospective: the Jacobian-lens output is flat (kurtosis 3.17, 0 of 10 tokens shared with the logit lens) and zero-ablating the pole moves next-token probabilities by KL 1.7e-5.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
Dear shareholders, partners and colleagues,

The past year has tested every part of our business, and I am pleased to report that we met the challenge with discipline and purpose. Revenue grew by nine percent to 4.2 billion, operating margin improved in every region, and we returned 610 million to shareholders through dividends and buybacks. These results reflect the effort of more than eighteen thousand employees who chose, every day, to put the customer first.

We entered the year with a clear plan: simplify the product range, shorten the time between a customer request and a delivered order, and hold the line on costs without compromising the quality our customers expect. We closed four legacy facilities, consolidated distribution into three regional hubs, and invested 240 million in automation at our largest plants. Lead times fell from eleven days to four, and on-time delivery reached 96 percent by the fourth quarter. The savings allowed us to absorb higher freight costs without raising list prices for the second year running.

None of this would have been possible without the trust of our partners. We renegotiated supply agreements with twelve of our fifteen largest vendors, extended payment terms where it made sense for both sides, and introduced a supplier code of conduct that every vendor has now signed. Where a relationship could not be repaired, we ended it respectfully and found a replacement before the next quarter opened. Our procurement team now reviews every contract worth more than fifty thousand against that code, and reports exceptions to the audit committee each month.

Our commitment to the communities in which we operate is unchanged. We donated 18 million to local education programmes, reduced water use at our manufacturing sites by 27 percent against a 2019 baseline, and completed the electrification of our own vehicle fleet ahead of schedule. The board has asked management to publish a full sustainability report each spring, and we intend to do so for the first time this April.

Looking ahead, the board believes that operational excellence is the foundation on which our next phase of growth will be built. We are not the largest company in our sector, and we do not need to be. We intend to be the one that customers recommend, that employees are proud to join, and that shareholders can rely on through the cycle. Every decision we take in the coming year will be measured against that standard. We will keep investing in the systems and the people that make that standard achievable, even in quarters when the headline numbers are less flattering.

On behalf of the board, I want to thank our employees, our customers and our shareholders for their continued confidence. We will report to you again in the spring.
